open_questions.q: How sensitive is the paper's HybASM > IllumASM > MinIONASM ranking to hybrid-assembler choice (Unicycler vs Trycycler vs hybridSPAdes)?
open_questions.basis: The paper uses Unicycler exclusively for both IllumASM and HybASM. Unicycler's hybrid mode is known to prefer conservative bridging, which can under- or over-count plasmids relative to Trycycler (which builds long-read consensus first from multiple Flye/Miniasm/Raven runs) or hybridSPAdes (SPAdes with Nanopore long-read scaffolding). Our replication could not test this because we did not do hybrid assembly at all; but the paper's conclusions about plasmid count and blaTEM/blaSHV variant discovery could shift materially under a different hybrid assembler.
next_steps: Re-run all 9 isolates through Trycycler + Polypolish and hybridSPAdes in addition to Unicycler hybrid, on the same PRJEB45084 reads.
Compare per-isolate plasmid replicon counts, total assembly length, N50, and ResFinder AMR gene counts across the three hybrid assemblers.
Report which conclusions (plasmid closure count, unique blaTEM/blaSHV variants) are stable across assemblers and which are Unicycler-specific artefacts.

open_questions.q: What is the minimum ONT coverage depth required to reliably close plasmids in HybASM for E. coli and K. pneumoniae clinical isolates?
open_questions.basis: The paper reports HybASM recovers 11 (E. coli) and 16 (K. pneumoniae) plasmids across 4+5 isolates, but does not systematically vary ONT coverage. Sub-sampling ONT reads to progressively lower depths and re-running Unicycler hybrid would establish a coverage-vs-closure curve. This is critical for sequencing-cost planning in clinical labs, where MinION Flongle flow cells produce far less data than a full MinION run. Our replication had no hybrid data at all, so this question is completely open.
next_steps: Sub-sample MinION reads for each isolate to 100x, 60x, 40x, 25x, 15x, and 10x estimated coverage.
Re-run Unicycler hybrid at each depth and count fully circularised plasmids (Bandage confirmation).
Report minimum coverage for 50%, 80%, and 100% plasmid closure per species; note whether small plasmids (<10 kb) close at lower coverage than large ones (>50 kb).

open_questions.q: How much of the MinIONASM 27.7% BUSCO complete score is a Guppy v3 / R9.4.1 artefact versus an inherent long-read-only limitation?
open_questions.basis: The paper's MinIONASM used R9.4.1 chemistry with Guppy v3 basecalling (2020-era). Since then, R10.4.1 chemistry with Dorado SUP basecalling has pushed nanopore-only assembly BUSCO scores above 95% for well-studied bacteria. The paper's damning MinIONASM verdict may be a snapshot of 2020 technology rather than a durable statement. Re-basecalling the paper's raw fast5/pod5 (if still available) with Dorado SUP and re-assembling would isolate the basecaller/chemistry contribution.
next_steps: Check whether raw ONT signal data (fast5/pod5) is available for PRJEB45084 --- ENA typically holds fastq only; if fast5 is not deposited, contact authors.
If pod5/fast5 available, re-basecall with Dorado SUP v0.7+ and re-assemble with Flye/Trycycler; recompute BUSCO.
If only fastq available, sequence a representative subset of the isolates fresh on R10.4.1 and compare BUSCO/QUAST to the paper's 2020 numbers.
Report the delta attributable to (basecaller + chemistry) vs the residual gap that reflects intrinsic long-read-only limitations.

open_questions.q: Does HybASM's advantage over IllumASM hold uniformly for plasmids and chromosomes, or is the improvement concentrated in the plasmid fraction?
open_questions.basis: The paper reports better resolution of plasmids, AMR genes, and virulence factors --- but AMR/VF genes are disproportionately plasmid-borne in ESBL Enterobacterales. It is not clear from the paper's tables whether HybASM meaningfully improves chromosomal assembly quality (contiguity, gene call accuracy) or whether the improvement is essentially all plasmid-driven. This matters for cost-benefit: if the chromosome assembles equally well with short reads alone, hybrid sequencing might only be worth the extra cost for isolates with unresolved plasmid content.
next_steps: For each isolate, separate contigs into chromosomal (aligned to reference chromosome, long single contigs) and plasmid (short contigs + PlasmidFinder hits + Bandage circularisation) fractions.
Compute per-fraction N50, misassembly rate (QUAST), and BUSCO completeness for IllumASM vs HybASM.
Report the improvement delta separately for chromosome and plasmid fractions; test the hypothesis that HybASM's chromosomal improvement is small relative to its plasmid improvement.

open_questions.q: How well do the paper's assembly-strategy conclusions generalise to a broader collection of ESBL/carbapenemase-rich clinical isolates beyond the 9-isolate NOR-KLEB cohort?
open_questions.basis: The paper's sample is 9 bloodstream isolates from Norwegian hospitals, representing a specific and relatively narrow slice of clinical Enterobacterales diversity (limited to particular ST types, plasmid types, and resistance profiles). Global ESBL/CPE surveillance (e.g., NDM-, KPC-, OXA-48-carrying Enterobacterales from South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America) covers a much wider range of large mosaic plasmids and integron cargo. It is unknown whether HybASM's advantage scales linearly, sub-linearly, or super-linearly with plasmid complexity/AMR gene count per isolate.
next_steps: Assemble a diverse benchmark set of 50-100 ESBL/CPE isolates with both Illumina and ONT data (candidates: NCBI Pathogen Detection PDG accessions, JPIAMR benchmark sets, EuSCAPE collection).
Stratify by carbapenemase class (KPC, NDM, VIM, IMP, OXA-48) and plasmid complexity score.
Run the same three-assembly pipeline (IllumASM/MinIONASM/HybASM) and report AMR gene recovery, plasmid closure rate, and variant-call precision as a function of resistance-cargo complexity.
Test whether the paper's plasmid recovery delta (HybASM 11+16 vs IllumASM 3+2) scales in isolates with 3+ AMR-carrying plasmids.
